title: HeteGen: Efficient Heterogeneous Parallel Inference for Large Language Models on Resource-Constrained Devices
problem: Large language models require substantial computational and memory resources, making inference on resource-constrained edge devices (mobile, IoT, embedded systems) infeasible with single hardware accelerators. Existing inference systems cannot efficiently leverage multiple heterogeneous hardware resources simultaneously on such devices.
motivation: Enabling efficient LLM inference on resource-constrained devices allows edge deployment, reduces latency, improves privacy, and minimizes energy consumption compared to cloud inference.
method: HeteGen runs large language models on resource-constrained devices like phones by splitting the computational work across available hardware accelerators—CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs. Rather than sending all the work to one chip, it dynamically decides at runtime which operations go to which hardware based on what each chip handles fastest. A scheduling layer coordinates execution and communication between the chips, keeping them all working in parallel to avoid idle time and delays.
key_novelty: HeteGen speeds up large language model predictions on phones and other resource-limited devices by dynamically splitting work across different hardware accelerators (CPU, GPU, NPU) so they all run in parallel.
contributions: Heterogeneous parallel inference framework for LLMs on resource-constrained devices
Intelligent workload partitioning strategy across CPU, GPU, and specialized accelerators
Scheduling and synchronization mechanisms for coordinating multi-hardware execution
Experimental validation showing speedups on edge devices with limited memory and compute
limitations: Not discussed (paper analyzed from title only).
primary_theme: Heterogeneous parallel LLM inference on resource-constrained edge devices
